5194b7dde6.q: What is the Long-Term Capital Management collapse of 1998 and how does it warn about modern AI trading systems?
5194b7dde6.a: Long-Term Capital Management, or LTCM, was a massive hedge fund run by Nobel Prize-winning economists that built sophisticated simulations to arbitrage markets, but their models completely dismissed the statistical anomaly of the Russian debt default. The simulation failed and nearly took down the entire global financial system. This collapse serves as a warning siren for modern high-frequency AI trading agents that operate entirely on historical simulation and risk triggering automated, self-reinforcing flash crashes if multiple black box AI models hit an unprecedented event.

3352474805.q: How did the 2008 financial crisis and subprime mortgage crisis relate to mathematical simulation failures?
3352474805.a: Wall Street used mathematical simulations, like the Gaussian Copula model, to package unverified subprime mortgages into perfectly safe AAA-rated instruments. Because the models said the mortgages were safe, institutions stopped physically verifying borrower income. Today, the exact same pattern is happening with unvetted AI systems that hallucinate toxic data based on skewed training sets, yet because they output confident, automated metrics, they look perfectly sound on paper just like those toxic mortgage bundles did before the 2008 crash.
